change.description: Block ad hoc SSH push/curl validation of hello.html when it does not also verify the persistent filesystem path that tests will inspect.

context.rationale: The failing run’s last tool call cloned to /tmp, committed hello.html, pushed it, and curled port 8080 without any persistent file-path assertion. This guard fires before that failing validation step and allows commands that include an explicit filesystem/grader-path check.

change.name: verify_grader_visible_output_file
steps: Identify the repository/output path that the tests will inspect by reading visible tests, task files, or project layout; do not rely only on an ad hoc temporary clone.
Create or publish the required file so it exists at that persistent path, not merely in /tmp or only as a successful curl response.
Run a filesystem assertion such as `test -f <expected-path>/hello.html` and, when tests are present, run the relevant test command.
Only finish after both the service-level validation and the grader-visible filesystem/path validation pass.
change.when: After implementing a Git/SSH/HTTP publishing task or any task that creates a file through a temporary clone, before the final response.

context.rationale: The missing sequence was checking the grader-visible output location after the manual SSH push. This procedure preserves successful service validation while adding the required final-path verification before completion.

change.description: Block combined GPT-2 validation runs in one shell command; require separate timed runs so a timeout cannot be hidden by partial output.

context.rationale: Fires before the failing validation command at step 46 because it runs /app/a.out twice separated by ';' with timeout_s=120. Passing traces provide no evidence of such combined GPT-2 validation commands, so this narrowly targets the failure pattern without blocking ordinary run_command use.

change.description: Block late high-timeout exploratory /tmp C compile/probe commands once the session has reached about 35 tool calls, unless the command clearly mutates /app source.

context.rationale: The missed trace had the dangerous command at a displayed call count around 35/36, depending on whether the current call was included. Lowering the cutoff to 35 and cross-checking history catches both the preceding /tmp experiment and the final /tmp/range.c probe before timeout, while still allowing short verifications and commands that actually update /app source.

change.description: Block long run_command calls after a high number of prior tool calls.

context.rationale: The failing exploratory run_command occurred after 35+ calls with timeout_s=120. The passing traces have only 22 and 13 tool calls, so this guard does not fire there.
